Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma on
11 December, 2024
 Honourable Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1435 Of 2018
Judgment:

sentences.text:
Aggrieved by the judgment dated 16.03.2017 (hereinafter will be referred as 'impugned judgment')
passed by the learned III Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Courts, Hyderabad (hereinafter will be referred as 'Tribunal') in O.P.No.1874 of 2014, the insurance company/respondent No.2 has filed the present Appeal to set aside the impugned judgment.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter are referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case as can be seen from the record are that the petitioners have filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondent Nos.1 and 2 for the death of deceased by name "Krishnaiah" (hereinafter will be referred as 'deceased').
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner Nos.2 to 5 are the children of the deceased.

The reason assigned by the petitioners for the death of the deceased is that on 23.05.2014 while the husband of the petitioner No.1 was waiting for an Auto near Ambedkar statue situated at Chinthapally 'X' Road, Chintapally Mandal, Nalgonda District at MGP,J about 10:00PM, one poultry lorry bearing No. AP.28.TC.5601 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner with high speed dashed to the deceased and ran over from the waist of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased received multiple injuries and died on the spot.

4. Based on the information received, Police, Chintapally Mandal, Nalgonda District registered a case in First Information Report (FIR) No. 87 of 2014 for the offence under Section 304-A of the Indian Penal Code, 1806 against the driver of crime vehicle and after completion of investigation filed charge sheet against the driver and owner of the crime vehicle.
5.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 53 years and he was engaged in agricultural works and used to earn Rs, 2,40,000/- per annum.

Therefore, the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-(Rupees Ten Lakhs) against the respondent Nos. 1 & 2, who are the owner and insurer of the crime vehicle bearing No. AP 28 TC 5601, for the death of the deceased under different heads.

6. Before the learned Tribunal, the respondent No.1/owner of the crime vehicle filed the counter denying the manner of MGP,J accident and contended that the driver of the crime vehicle never drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner; complainant is not an eye witness to the accident;
respondent driver is falsely implicated and thus, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

7. The respondent No. 2/Insurance Company filed counter denying the averments of the claim petition, the manner in which the accident occurred, the age, avocation, income of the deceased and Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36902466/
1 that the driver of the alleged crime vehicle was not hold a valid driving licence at the time of accident.

entities.text: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was also contended that the owner of the crime vehicle has not taken steps to inform Insurance Company soon after the accident as per Section 170 (a) and (b) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.
Therefore, on the above grounds the insurance company assailed the liability to pay any compensation amount.

It was further contended that the compensation claimed is excessive,
exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of the case.

8. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
a) Whether the accident in question took place on 23.05.2014 on account of the rash and negligent driving of the Poultry Lorry bearing No MGP,J AP.28.TC.5601 by its driver causing death of the deceased?

b) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
c) To what relief?
9.
On behalf of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW1 apart from examining PWs 2 and 3 and relied upon documentary evidence under Exs. A-1 to A-7.

On behalf of the respondents, none were examined but copy of insurance policy was marked as Ex. B1.
10.

The learned Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, partly allowed the claim petition in favour of the petitioners/claimants and making respondent Nos.1 and 2 liable to pay the compensation of Rs.9,37,850/- jointly and severally from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
Aggrieved by the impugned judgment, the respondent No.2/Insurance Company has preferred the present Appeal to set aside the impugned judgment.

11. Heard learned Standing Counsel for the appellant Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel for respondents/petitioners and perused the entire material available on record including the grounds of Appeal.
MGP,J 12.

The first and foremost contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the Tribunal ought to have dismissed the petition against the respondent No.2/Insurance Company on the ground that without any cogent evidence to establish income of the deceased the learned Tribunal erred in taking notional income of Rs.5,500/- as monthly income.

Further, it was contended that the deceased was an agriculturist that falls under the category of self employment but the learned Tribunal ought not to have granted 30% future prospects as in the case of Government employees with fixed income.

It is also the contention of the learned counsel for appellant that the learned Tribunal without considering the age of the deceased i.e., between 51 to 55 years, has wrongly applied '11' as multiplier instead of '9' that has been categorically held in catena of decisions by this Court and the Honourable Supreme Court.

Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36902466/
2 13.

entities.text: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Furthermore, the learned counsel contended that the Tribunal erroneously came to the conclusion without considering the age of the petitioners No. 2 to 4 and held that the petitioners No.
2 to 4 are dependent solely on the income of the deceased, accordingly deducted 1/4th towards the personal expenses of the deceased from the monthly income.

Therefore, on the above contentions the learned Standing Counsel for MGP,J appellant Insurance Company, prayed to allow the Appeal by setting aside the Decree and Judgment passed by the learned Tribunal.

14. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for respondents/claimants contended that the learned Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record has granted compensation,
which does not warrants for any interference of this court.

However, the learned counsel also contended that the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the income of deceased, who was an agriculturist, as Rs.10,000/- per month instead of taking notional income of Rs.5,500/- by considering the evidence of PW-3 and Ex. A-7 while assessing the income of the deceased.
On the above contentions, the learned counsel for respondents prayed to enhance the compensation by granting just and reasonable compensation.

15. Now the point for consideration is:
'Whether the Decree and Award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants any interference of this court?' MGP,J 16.
It is pertinent to note that the respondents/claimants have not filed any Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

17. A perusal of impugned Award discloses that the learned Tribunal having framed Issue No.1 as 'Whether the accident in question took place on 23.05.2014 on account of the rash and negligent driving of the Poultry Lorry bearing No AP.28.TC.5601 by its driver causing death of the deceased?'
to which the Tribunal after considering the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 coupled with documentary evidence under Exs.A1 (FIR), A2 (Charge-sheet), A3 (inquest report), A4 (Post Mortem Report), A5 (Scene of offence Panchanama) and A6 (Motor Vehicle Inspection Report) has answered issue No.1 holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the poultry lorry bearing No.
AP.28.TC.5601 and that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
There is also no dispute that the insurance policy under Ex.B1 was subsisting as on the date of accident.
There is also no dispute with regard to the relationship between the deceased and the claimants.
Thus, the above view of learned Tribunal in so far as manner of accident is considered does not warrants any interference of this court.
MGP,J 18.
In so far as quantum of compensation is concerned, according to the respondents/petitioners the deceased was aged 53 years, engaged in agricultural works and used to earn Rs.2,40,000/- per annum.

However, since the respondents/petitioners have not produced any documents except Ex.A-7 lease agreement entered between PW-3 owner of agricultural land and the deceased, who was a cultivator to the said agricultural land show that the deceased was earning Rs.2,40,000/-per Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36902466/

entities.text: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 annum, the learned Tribunal after taking into consideration Ex.A-7 and evidence of PW-3 has categorically observed that there was no documentary evidence to support the oral evidence of PW-3.

Hence, took the income of the deceased on notional basis as Rs.5,500/- per month, which seems to be just and reasonable, as such, there is no need to interfere with the findings of the Tribunal, so far as the earning capacity of the deceased is concerned.

19. Although the learned Standing Counsel for Insurance Company relied upon the decision of Honourable Supreme Court in General Manager, Kerala S.R.T.C vs Susama Thomas 1 to contend that the Tribunal erred in applying wrong multiplier of '11' by considering the age of the 1 1994 SCC (2) 176 MGP,J deceased as 53 years, there is no dispute with regard to the age of the deceased as '53'
years as evident from Exs.A1 to A4.

entities.text: General Manager, Kerala S.R.T.C vs Susama Thomas
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the principle laid down in Sarala Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 2, the appropriate multiplier for the persons aged between 51 to 55 years is '11'.

entities.text: Sarala Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As can be seen from the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier '11'
considering the age of the deceased.
Thus, this Court is of the considered view that the Tribunal rightly applied appropriate multiplier; hence, the contention of the appellant is unsustainable.
20. The learned Tribunal has taken monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 5,500/-.

Since the claimants are 5 in number, 1/4th of the monthly salary of the deceased (Rs.1,375/-) towards personal expenses of the deceased, as such, the contribution of the deceased towards his family members will arrive to Rs.4,125/-.

Since the deceased was aged 53 years and was self employed,
therefore, he is entitled for future prospects of 10% as per the decision laid down in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 3.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income of the deceased with future prospects comes to 2 (2009) 6 SCC 121 3 2017 ACJ 2700 MGP,J Rs.4,538/- per month (Rs.4,125/- + Rs.413/-) and the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.54,456/- (4,538/- x 12 months).
As stated above, the relevant multiplier for the age of the deceased is '11'.
When the annual salary of the deceased after deducting his personal expenses is multiplied with the relevant multiplier, it comes to Rs.5,99,016/- (Rs.54,456/- x 11).
Thus, the loss of dependency on account of sudden demise of deceased is Rs. 5,99,016/-.

Thus,
the loss of dependency on account of sudden demise of deceased is being reduced from Rs.7,07,850/- to Rs.5,99,016/-.
21.

The learned Tribunal erred in granting an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium,
Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of love and affection and Rs.30,000/- towards Transport, funeral and miscellaneous expenses.

It is settled principle of law in respect of granting compensation under conventional heads as per the principle laid down in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others 4 the claimants are entitled to Rs.77,000/- under the conventional heads (Rs.70,000/- + 10% enhancement thereon).

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in all, 4 2017 ACJ 2700 MGP,J petitioners/claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.6,76,016 /- (Rs.5,99,016/- + Rs. 77,000/-).

22. In view of the above facts and circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that impugned Award passed by the learned Tribunal is required to be modified to the extent of above observations.

Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36902466/
4 23.

entities.text: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co ... vs M Laxmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the result, the Appeal is allowed in part.

The quantum of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is hereby reduced from Rs.9,37,850/- to Rs.6,76,016/- with interest at 7.5% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of realization, to be payable by respondent No.1 (owner of the crime vehicle) and appellant/respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) jointly and severally.

The appellant/respondent No.2 Insurance Company and respondent no.1 (owner of crime vehicle) are directed to deposit the amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

Out of the above said compensation, the respondent No.1, wife of the deceased is awarded an amount of Rs.3,96,016/- and the petitioner Nos.2 and 5 being the son of the deceased are awarded an amount of Rs.70,000/- each.
On such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount awarded to them without MGP,J furnishing any security in the same proportion as apportioned above.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
